title: Advancing Confidence Calibration and Quantification in Medication Recommendation

problem.claim: Medication recommendation is a high-risk healthcare scenario in which confidence reliability matters.

gap.claim: Existing medication recommendation approaches face overconfidence in raw confidence for individual medications and lack a robust solution for quantifying confidence in medication combinations.

contributions.claim: A binning-based calibration method for individual-medication confidence with theoretical guarantees.
A sample-based method for quantifying confidence in medication combinations that applies to various existing medication-recommendation performance metrics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the binning-based method guarantees distinct accuracy levels between adjacent bins and maintains consistent statistical reliability across calibration and test data.
Using representative deep medication-recommendation models and MIMIC datasets, the authors report empirical effectiveness and robustness of the proposed methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Medication recommendation has advanced rapidly because of its practical healthcare implications.
High-risk medication recommendation still has overconfidence in individual-medication confidence and inadequate confidence quantification for combinations.
The authors describe the work as the first in-depth study of this gap.
The paper introduces binning-based calibration for individual medications and sample-based confidence quantification for medication combinations.
Experiments on deep medication-recommendation models and MIMIC datasets are reported to show effectiveness and robustness, with implications for clinical decision-making.

source_observation.claim: Confidence for individual medications and confidence for medication combinations are treated as distinct calibration or quantification problems.

interpretation.claim: Reliability methods may need to match the structure of the prediction target rather than apply one confidence treatment uniformly.

application.claim: For other multi-output recommendation systems, consider separate reliability procedures for component-level predictions and set- or combination-level predictions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation is necessary or effective outside medication recommendation.

source_observation.claim: The proposed individual-medication calibration method uses bins with distinct accuracy levels and consistent statistical reliability across calibration and test data.

interpretation.claim: Confidence calibration can be evaluated through both local ordering or separation properties and stability across data splits.

application.claim: When calibrating confidence in high-risk recommendation systems, assess bin-level behavior and calibration-to-test consistency.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the theoretical assumptions, calibration procedure, or guarantees' scope.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets' exact tasks, sizes, or preprocessing.
The abstract does not identify the representative deep medication-recommendation models or performance metrics used.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or comparisons with baselines.
The abstract does not detail the theoretical guarantees or limitations of either method.
